content.content:
Hires-By-The-Season: "I am Hires-By-The-Season, the root-herald of Low-Reed Village. I speak for our people to strangers, and I have little reason to trust anyone from Lilmoth. The Hist is the great tree our people hold sacred. Its eggs hatch in the pool at its roots. Eleven nights ago its light went out and its leaves shut. The eggs in the pool died. Our people say the leeches came up the roots. Then the tree shut. They blame Pays-Late too, the tree-minder who keeps the tree, because he let the leeches in. He stands by the roots under the stilts on the south side of the village, day and night. He will not say why. If a stranger can get the truth out of him, let the stranger try."

The interior, the villages inland behind the marsh, must hear that difference. The people who can carry it home gather at Helstrom, a great city behind the marsh. They are the tree-minders, who tend each village's Hist, and the Nisswo, wandering priests who read what a Hist says. I want them to hear what a cut tree looks like from someone the Reed can deny. So you go alone, and I send no escort. Do not name the Reed in Helstrom. If it is named, what you saw becomes the Reed's word and I cannot disown it. I do not like using a hand I can disown. I have no other. Take the coast ship at Lilmoth's stop, on the east side of the town. The ship has a door that opens on Helstrom's landing. Go ashore by it. From the landing the way runs inland over roots and through shallows. Two giant wasps keep the far bend of it, short of the gate. Just inside the gate, to the west, is the grove. Ei-Tuja stands there, a Nisswo who reads for anyone. Kaska-Meen is a tree-minder who sits in the city's assembly and keeps the grove's watch, and she hears few strangers. Whoever you tell decides how the word travels. A Nisswo preaches it in every village, where the cutters will hear it too. A tree-minder carries it only to those who keep trees.
